outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Cost Crisis in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces students to the fundamental motivation behind 1-bit LLMs. It explains the growing challenges in deploying large language models, including memory constraints, latency issues, and environmental costs. Students will understand why traditional approaches to model compression are insufficient and why a paradigm shift is necessary.
subtopics: The rise of Large Language Models and their computational demands
The scaling problem: why bigger models create deployment challenges
Memory footprint issues: DRAM to SRAM transfer costs
Energy consumption and environmental impact of LLMs
The fundamental limit: power as the bottleneck to compute performance

outline.description: This chapter provides essential background knowledge on quantization techniques. Students will learn about existing approaches to reducing model precision, understand their limitations, and build the foundation for understanding why training 1-bit models from scratch is a superior approach.
subtopics: What is quantization? From FP16/BF16 to lower precision
Post-training quantization: techniques and methods (GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant)
Why post-training quantization is sub-optimal
The progression: 16-bit → 4-bit and the trade-offs
Training with quantization vs. quantizing after training
Introduction to BitNet: the original 1-bit architecture

outline.description: Before diving into BitNet b1.58, students need to understand the original BitNet architecture. This chapter explains the core concepts of binary neural networks, the computational advantages of 1-bit weights, and how BitNet revolutionizes matrix multiplication operations.
subtopics: Binary neural networks: weights as {-1, +1}
Replacing floating-point multiplication with integer addition
The BitLinear layer architecture
Memory advantages: capacity and bandwidth reduction
Computational paradigm shift: from FLOPs to integer operations
Energy savings from simplified arithmetic

outline.description: This chapter provides a comprehensive explanation of the BitNet b1.58 architecture. Students will learn about the key innovation—ternary weights {-1, 0, 1}—and understand why adding the value 0 significantly improves modeling capability. The chapter covers the complete architecture including quantization functions and LLaMA integration.
subtopics: From binary to ternary: understanding the {-1, 0, +1} weight representation
Why '1.58 bits'? Understanding information-theoretic terminology
The significance of 0: explicit feature filtering
BitLinear layer design and implementation
Training from scratch: the quantization-aware training paradigm
8-bit activations: balancing precision and efficiency

outline.description: This chapter provides detailed mathematical treatment of the quantization functions used in BitNet b1.58. Students will learn the specific formulas for weight and activation quantization, understand the absmean quantization approach, and see how these functions are implemented in practice.
subtopics: Weight quantization: the absmean quantization function
Mathematical formulation: RoundClip and γ scaling
The rounding and clipping mechanism: constraining to {-1, 0, +1}
Activation quantization: per-token scaling
Eliminating zero-point quantization: scaling to [-Qb, Qb]
Comparison with original BitNet quantization approach

outline.description: This chapter explains how BitNet b1.58 integrates with the popular LLaMA architecture. Students will learn about each architectural component adopted from LLaMA and understand why this integration enables seamless adoption in the open-source ecosystem.
subtopics: LLaMA architecture as the open-source LLM backbone
RMSNorm: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization
SwiGLU activation function
Rotary embeddings (RoPE) for position encoding
Removing biases: simplification benefits
Integration with Huggingface, vLLM, and llama.cpp

outline.description: This chapter covers the experimental setup used to evaluate BitNet b1.58. Students will understand how fair comparisons are made between quantized and full-precision models, learn about the training data and benchmarks, and gain insight into proper evaluation methodology for LLMs.
subtopics: Training setup: RedPajama dataset and 100 billion tokens
Model sizes evaluated: from 700M to 70B parameters
Perplexity metrics: WikiText2 and C4 datasets
Zero-shot evaluation benchmarks (ARC, Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenbookQA, BoolQ)
Fair comparison principles: same size, same training tokens
Using lm-evaluation-harness for standardized evaluation

outline.description: This chapter presents and analyzes the key experimental results. Students will learn at what scale BitNet b1.58 matches full-precision performance, understand the performance-cost trade-offs, and see how the gap between quantized and full-precision models changes with model size.
subtopics: Perplexity comparison across model sizes
The 3B threshold: matching FP16 performance
BitNet b1.58 3.9B vs LLaMA 3B: better performance with lower cost
Zero-shot task accuracy analysis
Performance gap analysis: how the gap narrows with scale
2T token training results: comparison with StableLM-3B

outline.chapter_title: Efficiency Analysis: Memory, Latency, and Energy
outline.description: This chapter provides comprehensive analysis of the efficiency gains from BitNet b1.58. Students will learn how to measure and compare different efficiency metrics, understand the energy model for arithmetic operations, and see why efficiency advantages increase with model scale.
subtopics: Memory consumption: 3.55x reduction at 3B scale
Latency measurements: 2.71x speedup at 3B scale
Energy consumption analysis: FP16 operations vs INT8 additions
The 71.4x energy savings for matrix multiplication on 7nm chips
Scaling trends: why larger models benefit more
End-to-end energy cost analysis

outline.description: This chapter examines system-level performance metrics that matter for real-world deployment. Students will understand throughput measurements, batch size limitations, and how BitNet b1.58 enables more efficient hardware utilization.
subtopics: Throughput measurement methodology
Batch size scaling: 11x larger batch sizes
8.9x throughput improvement on 70B models
GPU memory limits and sequence length trade-offs
Pipeline parallelism and distributed inference
The 2-bit kernel optimization

outline.chapter_title: The New Scaling Law for LLMs
outline.description: This chapter introduces the new scaling paradigm enabled by BitNet b1.58. Students will understand the equivalence relationships between 1.58-bit and FP16 models, and learn how this changes the economics and design principles of large language models.
subtopics: Defining the new scaling law: performance vs. inference cost
Equivalence relationships: 13B 1.58-bit ≈ 3B FP16
Pareto improvement: better performance at lower cost
Implications for model design decisions
When to choose 1.58-bit over full-precision
Future-proofing LLM architectures

outline.chapter_title: Applications: MoE, Long Sequences, and Edge Deployment
outline.description: This chapter explores practical applications and extensions of BitNet b1.58. Students will learn how ternary quantization addresses key challenges in various deployment scenarios, from mixture-of-experts models to mobile devices.
subtopics: 1-bit Mixture-of-Experts: reducing memory and communication overhead
Native long sequence support: halving activation memory
KV cache compression opportunities
Edge and mobile deployment: overcoming memory and compute limitations
CPU-friendly execution for edge devices
Real-world deployment scenarios

outline.description: This chapter discusses the broader implications of 1-bit LLMs on hardware design and future research. Students will understand why current hardware is suboptimal for 1-bit models and envision the future of specialized AI accelerators.
subtopics: Current hardware limitations for 1-bit computation
The promise of specialized 1-bit hardware (LPUs and beyond)
Opportunities for system-level optimization
Open research problems in 1-bit LLMs
Combining 1.58-bit with other efficiency techniques
The future roadmap for efficient LLM architectures
